prologue_intro: ^Mother: Looks smaller than it did in the estate agent’s photographs.
^Mother: Jack, love, could you give us a hand with these boxes?

b: ^Mother: Just leave that one in the hall.
^Father: Good lad. We’ll manage the rest.

examine_window: ^Jack: You can see the cemetery from here.
examine_wardrobe: ^Jack: At least there’s plenty of room.

ask_mother: ^Jack: Can I have a look in the attic?
ask_father: ^Father: If the floorboards look rotten, keep off ’em.
^Father: And don’t go touching any wiring.

examine_old_speaker: ^Jack: He’d probably say this one’s still perfectly good.

b: ^Jack: That’s nice, but no batteries and someone’s snapped the aerial.
^Jack: Grandad would’ve tried fixing it. So will I.

examine_radio_first: ^Jack: That’s nice, but no batteries and someone’s snapped the aerial.
examine_radio_again: ^Jack: Grandad would’ve tried fixing it. So will I.

mother_shopping_quest: ^Jack: I’ll show you when it’s working.
^Mother: I need some milk, a loaf of bread, and some washing powder.
^Mother: Pop down to Store and bring those back.
^Mother: Whatever you’ve got left, you can keep.
^Mother: Don’t come back with a bicycle.

edith_intro: ^Edith: You’re the boy from the old Hale House.

introduction: ^Harris: You must be the new family.
^Harris: Son, I know everyone in Ashwick.

return_home: ^Mother: Don’t spend it all in one place.
radio_repair: ^Radio: I don’t know anymore. I thought no one would ever answer.
^Radio: Every word. You’re the first one who’s stayed. Thank you, Jack.
^Jack: I never told you my name.
radio_second_contact: ^Jack: How did you know my name?
^Radio: That's nothing to be ashamed of.
talk_to_father_about_radio: ^Jack: Dad, do you think radios can pick up...
^Father: Jack, give us a hand with this.
radio_after_father: ^Radio: You were going to tell him.
^Radio: I told you. I hear every word.
^Radio: Of course. He always seems busy when you’re talking.
^Radio: I shouldn’t judge someone I’ve never met. I just don’t like seeing you go quiet.
radio_next_morning: ^Radio: A corridor. Lockers. Chalk. Someone drawing by a window.
^Jack: You want me to go there?
^Radio: No. I don’t want you doing anything because I asked. You don’t owe me anything.
^Radio: I just thought…if I saw something familiar…maybe I’d remember my name.
emily_art_room_intro: ^Emily: You’re not supposed to be in here.
^Jack: Neither are you. What are you doing?
^Emily: It’s Ashwick. Someone sneezes and three streets know by teatime.
examine_emily_drawings: ^Emily: Sometimes I start with a room. Then there’s someone standing in it.
^Emily: Absolutely not. Makes the drawings better, though.
^Emily: Actually… Have you seen a blue sketchbook?
^Emily: I left it here yesterday. Which is impressive… seeing as I’ve already looked in here three times.
examine_mh_locker: ^Radio: I don’t know. I wish I did.
examine_school_camera: ^Emily: You’re asking the girl who’s currently trespassing. I’m probably not the authority.
play_school_recording: ^Radio: I don’t know. But when she said it… it hurt.
first_echo_point_appears: ^Radio: The sign. Come closer. Look at it.
open_mh_locker: ^Jack: ‘Don’t answer when it knows your name.’
^Radio: Then perhaps… you shouldn’t talk to me.
^Radio: If you think I’m dangerous… turn me off. I won’t stop you.
radio_after_returning_sketchbook: ^Radio: She knew you weren’t telling the truth.

start: ^Mother: I’m looking for a little brass key.
^Mother: It should be in one of the kitchen boxes.
david_warning: ^David: The floor might not be safe.
radio_warning: ^Jack: Why does that sound like a challenge?
return_key: ^Mother: Your father told you to stay out of there.
^Mother: And I’m trying to keep you safe.
radio_afterward: ^Radio: Of course. She just has a quiet way of showing it.

start: ^Father: Jack. Could you pop down and buy a replacement fuse? I’ll pay you back.
radio_afterward: ^Radio: Like he wasn’t expecting you to.

start: ^Edith: Jack, dear? Would you have a look around for me?
^Edith: I used to have a little music box. I do wonder whatever became of it…
radio_afterward: ^Radio: Maybe I was. Does it matter …if nobody remembers?

examine_ledger: ^Radio: He took my money. Smiled at me. Probably called me ‘son’.
confront_harris: ^Harris: …That’s my handwriting, but why would I write down a name…
^Harris: Where did you get that Radio?
^Harris: Hale House… I hoped nobody would ever switch that thing on again.
^Harris: I don’t know. Some things are better left quiet.
^Harris: Bits of him. Always taking radios apart.
^Harris: I think I did. I just wish I remembered why.
^Harris: Jack… Whatever’s talking through that radio…
^Harris: Don’t mistake knowing you, for caring about you.
radio_afterward: ^Radio: Maybe. And you chose to fix it.
^Radio: When does it become someone’s fault, Jack?

start: ^Emily: I saw you talking to it.
^Emily: I never said there was anything wrong with that.
radio_before_drawing: ^Radio: Maybe. Would you tell her everything?
^Radio: What if she tells Harris? or your parents? They’d take me away.
^Radio: Then tell her. Go on. I trust you.
show_drawing: ^Emily: This was in my sketchbook this morning.
^Radio: I don’t know why. Looking at it makes me afraid.

c-0: ^Emily: Thanks. I thought you’d keep it.
^Emily: You’ve been keeping everything else to yourself.

after_choice: ^Radio: I trust you with my life.

encounter: ^Radio: He doesn’t get to order you.
^Finch: I helped this town forget him.
^Finch: I burned the record. Destroyed the photograph. Told his family to leave.
^Radio: And he wants you to trust him.
^Finch: I thought forgetting would weaken it. I was wrong. We only fed it.
^Finch: It’s the only one that matters.
radio_afterward: ^Jack: He was trying to stop you.
^Radio: Me? Jack… You think I’m the thing that did this?
^Jack: I don’t know what you are.
^Radio: Neither do I. I thought you were the one person , who didn’t need me to explain myself.
^Radio: You’re right. I’m sorry. Forget I said anything.
radio_returns: ^Radio: I didn’t want to bother you.
^Radio: I thought maybe you’d rather listen to Finch.
^Radio: So do I. Maybe that’s why we’re still together.

open_gates: ^Jack: He wants me to find your grave.
^Radio: Do you believe him? You needn’t decide yet.
examine_michael_grave: ^Jack: Is this where Finch trapped you?
first_face_to_face: ^Jack: You knew this place was here.
^Michael: Not at first. I remembered bits..
^Jack: Why do you sound like all those people?
^Michael: Finch used memories to keep me here.
^Jack: He said they kept the Echo shut.
^Michael: He called it a seal. A prison sounds kinder when you give it another name.
^Michael: Nothing you don’t choose for yourself.
^Michael: It belongs to the boy buried above us.
after_final_wave: ^Michael: I was scared. Take off the name and open the door.

begin: ^Michael: We can stop. No more fighting.
^Michael: Remove the name. Open the door. Nobody will ever have to be forgotten again.

b: ^Michael: That’s it. You opened the door.
^Michael: Your choice. Your hands. Your decision.
^Jack: Your song is remembered. Your face is remembered. Your name is still here. That’s enough.
^Jack: I’m sorry. But I can’t let you take anyone else.
